page: Amazon Web Services r6id.16xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by the Intel Xeon 8375C processor. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture, it features 64 virtual CPUs across 32 physical cores with hyper-threading, operating at a clock speed of 3.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 512.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per virtual core. It includes 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps, managed via the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 25% of tested systems. The processor's support for AVX-512 and cryptographic instructions contributes to strong performance in encryption and extended instruction tests. Database operations and static web serving throughput also rank in the top 25%, while memory bandwidth and single-core performance metrics remain in the average range.

Given the high density of DDR4 memory paired with substantial local NVMe SSD storage, this instance provides a balanced resource profile for data-intensive workloads without the need for external storage attachments. This makes it highly suitable for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching systems, data compilation, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
description: The Amazon Web Services r6id.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 64 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz. It is equipped with 512.0 GB of DDR4 memory, 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and a 25 Gbps baseline network interface, all running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Benchmark results show strong multi-core CPU performance, database operations, and static web serving throughput, while single-core and memory bandwidth metrics fall in the average range. The inclusion of high-capacity local NVMe storage alongside a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes this instance highly efficient for memory-intensive and storage-heavy workloads. It is well-suited for hosting large databases, software compilation, and in-memory caching applications.
